## Findings ledger
- [C2.DOC1.F1] AUKUS answers what institutional mechanism it represents: it is presented as a security partnership and a mutation of neoliberalism in which bipartisanship reconnects business, political and military networks — dim: case_answers — anchor: "We argue that AUKUS is not simply a security partnership, but rather constitutes a mutation of neoliberalism emerging in the context of bipartisanship." — doc: aukus — criterion: What institutional mechanism does AUKUS represent? — value-kind: qualitative — evidence-role: conceptual claim — scope: AUKUS and its political-economic order — causal-attribution: AUKUS named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "The latter entails state transformation which reconnects business, politics, and military networks in new ways." — doc-b: aukus — case: AUKUS — causal-attribution: AUKUS named by the attributing sentence
- [C2.DOC1.F2] Australia answers how bipartisan support operates: it enables regulatory controls and policy tools that connect security cooperation to market coordination and benefit selected economic groups — dim: case_answers — anchor: "AUKUS, which connects responses from the political left and right to China, the Ukraine War, and the economic turmoil of neoliberal globalisation, serves as an institutional setting for promoting significant regulatory changes" — doc: aukus — criterion: How does bipartisan support operate institutionally? — value-kind: qualitative — evidence-role: mechanism — scope: Australia and AUKUS-related regulatory changes — causal-attribution: AUKUS named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "These regulatory changes and supporting policy tools undergird certain conceptions of development, including the development of advanced dual technologies and procurement of critical minerals" — doc-b: aukus — case: Australia — causal-attribution: regulatory changes and supporting policy tools named by the attributing sentence
- [C2.DOC1.F3] Australia answers what quantitative state-financing capacity is mobilised for critical minerals: the government unveiled an AUD 2 billion expansion in critical-minerals financing to support Australian and US manufacturing sectors — dim: case_answers — anchor: "the Australian Government unveiled an AUD 2 billion expansion in critical minerals financing not only to achieve net-zero goals, but also ‘supporting the Australian and United States’ manufacturing sectors’" — doc: aukus — criterion: What state-financing capacity is mobilised through the AUKUS economic-security nexus? — value-kind: quantitative — evidence-role: reported result — scope: Australian critical-minerals financing, 2023 — causal-attribution: Australian Government named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "This makes Australian suppliers of critical minerals and technologies eligible for US funds." — doc-b: aukus — case: Australia — causal-attribution: the Australia–United States Compact and US Congress are named by the attributing sentence
- [C2.DOC1.F4] South Korea answers how two separately named instruments relate to defence-export finance: a June 2023 statutory-capital proposal and a December 2023 Enforcement Decree are both reported, but the text does not establish that they are the same instrument or stages of one amendment — dim: case_answers — anchor: "In response to industry calls for legislative amendments, in June 2023 the government proposed to increase the lender’s statutory capital limit." — doc: aukus — criterion: What instrument changes are reported, and is their identity across stages established? — value-kind: qualitative — evidence-role: mechanism — scope: South Korean Eximbank financing and defence exports, June 2023 — causal-attribution: South Korean government named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "The revised Enforcement Decree of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act passed the National Assembly, coming into effect in December 2023" — doc-b: aukus — case: South Korea — causal-attribution: the revised Enforcement Decree named by the attributing sentence
- [C2.DOC1.F5] Australia answers what demonstrated implementation constraint affects Pillar I: severe delays in UK submarine-building and possible US congressional refusal may leave Australia without sovereign submarine capability for years — dim: case_answers — anchor: "severe delays emerging out of the devastating state of the UK submarine-building industry and the US Congress’s predisposition to deny the delivery of the submarine might result in few concrete results to show for years to come" — doc: aukus — criterion: What implementation constraint and reported consequence affect AUKUS Pillar I? — value-kind: qualitative — evidence-role: reported result — scope: AUKUS submarine capability, as reported in 2024 — causal-attribution: UK submarine-building delays and US Congress’s predisposition named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "leaving Australia with no sovereign submarine capability" — doc-b: aukus — case: Australia — causal-attribution: the reported delays and possible congressional refusal are the attributed conditions
- [C2.DOC1.F6] AUKUS Defense Investor Network answers what institutional capacity links venture capital to Pillar II: it brings together private venture capital funds worth USD 400 billion and seeks to expand defence collaboration in AI and quantum computing — dim: case_answers — anchor: "the AUKUS Defense Investor Network brings together private VCs worth 400 USD billion in funds from AUKUS countries" — doc: aukus — criterion: What financial and institutional capacity links venture capital to Pillar II? — value-kind: quantitative — evidence-role: mechanism — scope: AUKUS countries’ private venture capital network, established December 2023 — causal-attribution: AUKUS Defense Investor Network named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "the group seeks to broaden the focus of defence collaboration between the three countries to include advanced military technology such as AI and quantum computing under Pillar II." — doc-b: aukus — case: AUKUS Defense Investor Network — causal-attribution: the group named by the attributing sentence

scope_outcomes.criterion: The source must supply an attributable answer about an actor, instrument, mechanism, capacity, constraint, reported consequence, or conceptual definition relevant to comparing cases.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected sections provide six anchored answers concerning AUKUS’s institutional definition, bipartisan regulatory mechanism, Australian financing capacity, distinct South Korean instruments, submarine implementation constraints, and venture-capital capacity.
limitations: The source does not establish a common quantitative outcome or ranking standard across all named countries.
The identity of the June 2023 South Korean proposal and the December 2023 Enforcement Decree remains unresolved.
